headline: Aerospace strength drives a broad margin and profit surge
summary_short: RBC Bearings' fiscal Q1 2027 (three months ended June 27, 2026) revenue rose 19.2% y/y to $519.5 million as Aerospace & Defense sales jumped 36.9%, with gross margin expanding to 47.7% from 44.8% and diluted EPS climbing to $3.20 from $2.17.
summary_long: Aerospace & Defense sales rose 36.9% and Industrial rose 8.4%; $34.4 million came from the VACCO acquisition. Gross margin expanded to 47.7% (GAAP and adjusted) from 44.8%/45.4% on richer mix. Operating income rose 39.3% to $140.8 million as SG&A fell to 16.5% of sales despite an $11.9 million dollar rise. Interest expense fell on debt reduction; net income rose 48.2% to $101.5 million, diluted EPS to $3.20. Operating cash flow rose to $171.8 million; RBC repaid $77.0 million of term loans, yet cash still rose to $124.5 million from last quarter. Backlog held at $2.3 billion, up from $1.0 billion a year ago. For Q2 FY2027, RBC guides net sales of $505-515 million, gross margin 45.5-45.75%, SG&A 16.5-16.75%.

drivers.explanation: Aerospace & Defense sales rose 36.9% and Industrial rose 8.4%; $34.4 million of the increase came from the VACCO acquisition closed July 18, 2025.
Reflects favorable mix; adjusted gross margin also rose, to 47.7% from 45.4%, with $2.9 million less restructuring drag than a year ago.
Followed the sales and margin gains; SG&A rose $11.9 million in dollars but fell to 16.5% of sales from 16.9%, with other operating expense up only modestly.
Tracks the operating-income gain; interest expense fell to $10.1 million from $12.2 million on "continued debt reduction efforts," while the effective tax rate held near flat (22.1% vs 21.9%).
Grew in line with net income; diluted share count rose only slightly y/y (31.7M from 31.6M), so per-share growth closely tracked the profit gain.
Company-reported Adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 34.9% of net sales from 32.5%, tracking the same operating-margin and mix-shift gains already cited for gross and operating margin.
Rose largely on the higher net income plus favorable working-capital swings, including accrued liabilities up $34.0 million versus $25.5 million a year ago.
Fell y/y as $77.0 million of term-loan repayments and $24.9 million of capex outweighed the higher operating cash flow versus the year-ago balance.
Fell as the company continued repaying term loans this quarter ($77.0 million), consistent with management's stated "continued debt reduction efforts."
Rose on retained-earnings growth from net income, partly offset by $10.7 million of treasury-stock additions from tax withholding on equity awards.

Broad-based beat led by Aerospace & Defense strength, the VACCO contribution, and margin expansion; net income rose 48.2% and diluted EPS to $3.20. RBC guides Q2 FY2027 net sales of $505-515 million with margins roughly flat q/q.
